text: Four thousand dollars, up front. Their students scored higher.
Same bonus. The only change: when it was paid.
In 2010, nine schools near Chicago tested teacher bonuses.
One group could earn up to eight thousand dollars at the end of the year.
Another got four thousand on day one, and had to give some back if students fell short.
Same money for the same results.
End-of-year bonus? Math scores barely moved.
Money already in hand? Math jumped about seven percentile points.
Losing money hurts more than missing it.
That's why four thousand up front worked.
